newsitem.title: CHINA: Copyright pirates hijack China's Opium War epic.
newsitem.headline: Copyright pirates hijack China's Opium War epic.

text.p: Copyright pirates have hijacked China's costly movie epic of the Opium War, a centrepiece of its propaganda leading up to the Hong Kong handover.
"The Opium War', which cost HK$116.07 million (US$15 million) to make, is on sale for HK$30 (US$3.8) on an unlicensed compact disk just three days after the handover, a newspaper said.
Beijing took Hong Kong back from Britain at midnight on Monday, ending 156 years of colonial rule that began with China's humiliating defeat in the Opium War.
A youth selling the pirated film alluded to involvement of a higher authority when he was asked if he feared any penalty for depriving mainland Chinese film makers of royalties.
"If you knew who owned the factory which makes these disks, you'd know there is no problem", the South China Morning Post quoted him as saying.

The film, highly recommended by Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, tells the story of how Britain seized Hong Kong from imperial China after a Chinese official had burned opium peddled by the British.
The film was launched ahead of the handover to stoke Chinese patriotic feeling and remind Chinese and foreign audiences of Hong Kong's beginnings.
